title: improv·artist · watery (Vija Celmins)
mutation_directive: improv artist: watery via Vija Celmins

improv_extras.practice: graphite ocean surfaces, night skies; impossible patience

v1.feedback: The concentric differential-growth rings mapped to a gently undulating ocean plane is a legit Celmins translation — graphite-mark tubes with curvature-responsive thickness is a smart detail. The monochrome silver-on-near-black palette is restrained and correct. Two issues: the wave displacement is so subtle (±0.12 units) that at the default low camera angle the surface reads almost flat — bump the amplitude range 2-3× so the ocean texture is visible within 2 seconds without orbiting. Second, 9 rings at 600-vert cap each could be denser; consider 14-16 thinner rings packed tighter so the surface feels more like Celmins' obsessive all-over graphite field rather than isolated concentric loops with gaps.

v2.feedback: The concentric-ring layout reads as a bullseye more than a Celmins all-over ocean field — scatter ring centers across the plane or use a grid of short differential-growth strands so the density feels directionless like her graphite. MeshBasicMaterial kills depth: switch to MeshStandardMaterial with low roughness so the wave displacement actually produces tonal shifts across the surface, which is the whole point of Celmins' obsessive mark-making. Wave amplitudes (~0.75 total) are small relative to the 20-unit spread — double them or tighten the camera so the undulation is unmistakable at first glance.
